title: Add one server: hash mod N moves most keys, a hash ring moves one arc
captions: Method A: pick the server with hash(key) mod N. With 3 servers, key A has hash 12, and 12 mod 3 = 0, so it goes to S0.
You add a fourth server, so N becomes 4. Key B has hash 7, and 7 mod 4 = 3, so it moves from S1 to S3. B, C, D and F all change servers.
4 of 6 keys moved, and some moved between two old servers. On average, going from 3 to 4 servers moves 3 of every 4 keys.
Method B: a hash ring. Servers and keys are hashed to points on a circle. Each key belongs to the next server clockwise. So B and C belong to S1.
You add S3. It lands between S0 and S1, so it takes only the keys in that arc: just B. C is past S3, so it stays on S1.
Only B moved. With N servers, a new server takes about 1/(N+1) of the keys, and no key moves between two old servers.
